text.en: A bee visits a flower for nectar and leaves with pollen on its legs. Its next visit may start a new seed. Pollination is the first step in making a seed.

Pollination is the transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma; it leads to fertilization, fruits and seeds.
Self-pollination (autogamy) happens within the same flower or plant, as in Hibiscus; it needs no agent and wastes no pollen, but gives fewer seeds, weak plants and no new varieties.
Cross-pollination takes pollen to a flower on another plant of the same species; it gives healthy seeds and new varieties but depends on agents and wastes pollen.
Wind pollination (anemophily): flowers produce huge amounts of light, dry pollen and have large feathery stigmas, as in grasses.
Insect pollination (entomophily): flowers are colourful, scented and rich in nectar with sticky, spiny pollen; honey bees do about 80 percent of it.
Water pollination (hydrophily) occurs in aquatic plants such as Hydrilla and Vallisneria; animal pollination is zoophily, for example sunbirds pollinating Canna.
After landing on the stigma the pollen grain forms a pollen tube that grows through the style to the micropyle and releases two male gametes into the embryo sac.
One male gamete fuses with the egg (syngamy) to form the diploid zygote; the other fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion) to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.
Two fusions in one embryo sac are called double fertilization; the endosperm feeds the embryo and the synergids and antipodals degenerate.
After fertilization the ovule becomes the seed, the integuments become the seed coat and the ovary becomes the fruit.

problem.en: Compare self- and cross-pollination in terms of seed quality and variation.

text.en: Self-pollination gives fewer seeds with minute endosperm, so plants are weaker.
Cross-pollination mixes genes of two plants.
So only cross-pollination produces new varieties.

why.en: That is why it is more useful for evolution.

prompt.en: Describe the steps of double fertilization.

requiredIdeas.en: Pollen tube enters the embryo sac

points.en: Self- and cross-pollination; agents: wind, insects, water, animals.
Pollen tube carries two male gametes to the embryo sac.
Syngamy gives the zygote; triple fusion gives the endosperm.
Ovule becomes seed, ovary becomes fruit.
